transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-09 09:30 PDT
Duration: 45 min
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Acme PL), Marcus Chen (Acme ML Eng), Ellen Park (Acme SRE)

Summary (auto): quick sync on the pilot's throughput tuning; small wins from continuous batching, need to tune batch timeout and concurrency to balance p95.

[00:00] Samir: ok folks thanks for joining, we'll do a quick 45 minute sync, agenda is results, tuning experiments, and next steps. Lena will run through the numbers.
[00:22] Lena: cool, thanks. So since last week we ran three main experiments: baseline (no continuous batching), cb enabled with batch_timeout=10ms, and cb with prefix cache. The baseline avg tokens/sec was ~680, p95 latency at 750ms for 256-token responses under concurrency=8.
[00:45] Lena: with continuous batching at 10ms we saw tokens/sec jump to ~1,050 with p95 at 880ms, so throughput up but tail worse slightly. when we added prefix cache the tokens/sec moved to ~1,150 and p95 came down to 720ms, so cache helped the tail.
[01:10] Priya: wait, where are these runs—staging or dedicated? we thought the dedicated pool was isolated.
[01:18] Lena: staging on dedicated pilot pool, we kept model pinned to redwood-rlhf-7b-quant-v2 to match your evals. remember we had KV cash miss earlier—transcript note, the artifact where KV cache was cold caused some outliers.
[01:35] Marcus: i noticed a few spikes in the tail around 02:00 UTC; looks like prewarming didn't always hit. did you try pre-populating the KV cache?
[01:44] Lena: we did two prewarm passes but not full prefix coverage. the prefix cache feature is still warming; we saw around ~18% hit rate on average for the test set. with more targeted prompt sets we'd expect higher hit rate.
[02:05] Ellen: network wise, our infra team flagged occasional queue buildup when concurrency > 12, likely due to our ingress NLB settings plus some burst throttling.
[02:18] Priya: yeah, we're worried about queueing leading to request timeouts. what's Redwood recommending for queue timeouts and concurrency caps?
[02:25] Samir: good question. from our side, the pilot's sweet spot tends to be concurrency 10-14 for your prompt distribution. above that you get diminishing returns and increased tail. the knobs are: batch_timeout (ms), max_batch_size, and concurrency. lowering batch_timeout reduces per-request latency but may reduce batch sizes and hurt throughput.
[02:55] Lena: to add, continuous batching uses an ultra-low batch_timer to accumulate requests; at 10ms we saw good throughput. we tried 6ms briefly in a lab and throughput was still decent, but that was synthetic. Marcus, you could try 6ms in staging to measure real workload behavior.
[03:15] Marcus: yes we can run that. i'm concerned about quantized model compute variance; sometimes the GPU kernels have jitter at small batch sizes.
[03:25] Lena: noted—kernel jitter can increase tail, especially for dynamic shapes. we recommend enabling kernel fusion where possible and ensuring your dedicated nodes are on the same GPU family to avoid cross-instance variance.
[03:40] Priya: on cost—if we push concurrency up, cost goes up linearly? or batching makes cost per token lower?
[03:48] Samir: batching increases utilization and decreases per-token compute overhead, so cost per token typically drops with smarter batching. but concurrency increases the number of active sessions which can increase overall instance usage. our cost model in the spreadsheet shows diminishing marginal returns after concurrency ~14 for your workload. i'll send the updated numbers.
[04:10] Lena: also try the adaptive batching profile we discussed—it ramps batch_timeout dynamically based on incoming qps to hit latency SLOs. that gave the best p95/throughput tradeoff in our tests.
[04:25] Ellen: about queueing, do you recommend queue_length limit or backpressure at the ingress? we can't have huge request backlogs.
[04:33] Lena: set a short service-level queue (e.g., 100ms max wait) and let the client retry with jitter. Redwood can also reject with a 429 when queue exceeds threshold. This avoids long tails from head-of-line blocking.
[04:48] Marcus: any notes on autoscaling? our dedicated pool has autoscale but default cooldown was long and we saw capacity lag.
[04:56] Lena: reduce scale cooldown and use metric-based autoscaling on queued requests and GPU utilization; for tight SLOs use conservative cooldowns. we can help tune those thresholds.
[05:10] Priya: ok can we recap the concrete experiments we agreed to run this week?
[05:15] Samir: yes: 1) Marcus to run batch_timeout=6ms with concurrency=12 for 12 hours on staging (collect p50/p95/p99 and batch size distribution). 2) Lena to enable prefix cache and push config, monitor hit rate and warm-up. 3) Samir to share updated throughput + cost spreadsheet. 4) Ellen to check VPC peering / NLB queueing with infra.
[05:35] Priya: timeline? we'd like nightly runs and results by early next week.
[05:39] Samir: we'll aim to have experiment results by 2025-07-14 and the spreadsheet by 2025-07-11.
[05:47] Marcus: a quick question—what about model variants? could we try a slightly smaller quantized variant for high throughput tails?
[05:55] Lena: yes that's an option—redwood-rlhf-6b-qq (quant) tends to cut p95 by ~15% and token cost by ~20% in similar workloads, but evaluate output quality first. we can do side-by-side A/B on a canary route.
[06:15] Priya: that sounds good. also please include SLO dashboards for per-route p95 and cost per 1k tokens in the spreadsheet.
[06:23] Samir: will do. Lena also suggested adaptive batching; Marcus, do you want Redwood to push that profile or do you want to self-manage?
[06:31] Marcus: prefer Redwood to push the profile to staging and we'll observe.
[06:35] Lena: okay i'll push adaptive profile and the prefix cache config after this call.
[06:40] Ellen: one more thing—security asked for audit logs retention details and who can view logs. can you share the SOC2 scope doc again?
[06:48] Samir: yes i'll attach SOC2 and the audit logs doc in the follow up email.
[06:53] Priya: perfect. any other risks?
[06:56] Lena: main risks are prefix cache cold starts and kernel jitter at very small batch sizes. mitigation: targeted prewarm and co-locating GPU families.
[07:08] Samir: recap of next steps and owners (we'll post to the CRM thread): Marcus run 6ms/12c test (due 7/14), Lena enable prefix cache + adaptive batching (due 7/10), Samir share spreadsheet (due 7/11), Ellen check VPC peering (due 7/12).
[07:30] Priya: thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (KV cash -> KV cache, V-P-C spelled out). Links mentioned: shared throughput spreadsheet (link posted in CRM), SOC2 summary (link), prefix cache config snippet (gists).
